title: Inverse search mutates real training designs in timed rounds and scores the exact recipe it sends
context: 12-search-core.js decodes training seeds into recipes, varies them the way F13LD.sweep does (nudges within training ranges, sin/cos swaps, frequency changes), encodes and scores each one. Rounds grow from the current best and from the best in each cell of a 24×24 grid, with a shrinking step, under a time budget (00-config.js SEARCH_DEPTHS) on a worker pool (20-predictor.js).

options.name: Seeded mutation over real designs (current)
options.summary: Evolutionary search anchored to training seeds, scoring the exact design.
pros: Scored design and sent design are identical (v0.2 differed by a median 22 points)
Stays near the data the model knows
Grid keeps alternatives spread over the map
cons: Cannot find designs far from any seed

options.name: Optimize a continuous feature vector, then snap to a recipe
cons: Ranks a design it never sends; replaced in v0.3.0 for that reason

options.name: CMA-ES or Bayesian optimization over recipe parameters
options.summary: A formal optimizer on the decoded recipe space.
pros: Better sample efficiency on hard targets
cons: Mixed discrete and continuous structure (terms, trig choice) fits poorly

recommendation: README "Search over real designs" and "Rounds, by time" describe it and the v0.3.0 recap records why the snap approach was dropped; implemented in 12-search-core.js and worker/search-worker.js.
